newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 22.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The African National Congress has again called for the resignation of KwaZulu-Natal Attorney General Tim McNally after the withdrawal of charges on Wednesday against six Inkatha members arrested in connection with the attack on Zulu King Goodwill Zwelithini's palace last year. The charges were withdrawn after the murders of three witnesses in the case.

- Details of far-reaching changes plannes for the energy, mining and liquid fuel industries were outlined by Mineral and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna in his maiden speech in Parliament on Wednesday.

- Gencor Ltd has withdrawn from the consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd mulling over an investment in the $80 million Zambian copper resource Konkola Deep, citing a lower than expected rate of return, the South African group said on Wedensday.

- Alienated National Party Gauteng leader Roelf Meyer announced the establishment of a "new movement process" and a fundraising foundation on Wednesday as the first steps towards finding an alternative to the ANC.

- Recent fossil finds at Sterkfontein and other nearby sites backed up assertions that the Taung child was the missing link between man and ape, paleoanthropologist Professor Phillip Tobias said on Wednesday night.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Penuell Maduna, the mineral and energy affairs minister, revealed plans on Wednesday to consolidate all state-owned energy-related assets into a "major integrated energy company" to be listed on the JSE and to be used later as a tool for black economic empowerment.

- Telkom managers and executive committee members will not lose their jobs or positions to make way for new equity partner appointments, Dikgang Moseneke, the chairman and acting chief executive of Telkom, said on Wednesday.

- The rapid growth of the local pie industry, which has an annual turnover of 500 million rand, lies behind the pending listing of First SA Food Holdings, John Welch, the managing director of Piemans Pantry and First SA Food, said recently.

- Investec Group Ltd, the investment and private banking group, on Wednesday reported strong year-end results largely due to some smart shopping for acquisitions and growth in its asset management division, the bank said.

- The Steel and Engineering Industries Federation of South Africa (Seifsa) on Wednesday effectively agreed to six months' paid maternity leave, including the extension of the benefit to employees who were foster mothers of children under six months, said Brian Angus, Seifa's executive director.
SAKE BEELD
- Government is planning to merge all its petrol and oil interests in one large energy company, which it will listed as a public company on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
- Parliament will be asked to forbid credit cards to be issued to individual civil servants and employees of state- controlled corporations.
- Pyramid schemes will soon be officially prohibited by government, said Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin.
- For the second time in South Africa's history, bank officials will march through the country's streets -- this time in protest against the violence which bank robbers expose them to.
THE STAR

- A security guard was shot in the leg during a 10 million rand military-style heist on Wednesday after his security van was forced off the road by a gang of robbers on the N12 highway on the East Rand.
- National Party office bearers and elected representatives, who in the past publicly stated their support for Roelf Meyer, are being victimised, according to informed sources.

- President Mandela delivered a tough and uncompromising message to top international investors on Wednesday, saying southern Africa was "entitled" to investment from industrial countries because they had usbjected the region to "the most brutal form of exploitation" in the colonial era.
- Interpol agents will meet police detectives at Hoedspruit in the Northern Province on Monday to assist in the investigation into "canned" lion hunting in South Africa.
